tool.name: minibwa index
tool.description: Index a reference genome for minibwa alignment
tool.command:
ln -s '$reference_fasta' 'ref.fa' &&
minibwa index #if $low_memory: -l #end if -t \${GALAXY_SLOTS:-1} #if $meth: --meth #end if 'ref.fa' 'ref' &&
## Move index files to Galaxy output paths mv 'ref.l2b' '$index_l2b' && mv 'ref.mbw' '$index_mbw' #if $meth: && mv 'ref.meth.mbw' '$index_meth_mbw' #end if

param.label: Generate BS-seq index
param.help: Generate an additional index file for directional bisulfite sequencing (BS-seq) alignment

param.name: low_memory
param.label: Use low-memory BWT-SW algorithm
param.help: Use the slower but memory-efficient BWT-SW algorithm instead of the default libsais algorithm

tool.help:
# minibwa index
Minibwa is a short/long-read aligner that is the successor to BWA-MEM, combining BWA-MEM variable-length seeding with minimap2 chaining and base alignment.
This tool builds a genome index for use with **minibwa map**.
## What it produces
- **`.l2b` file** — 2-bit encoded reference genome - **`.mbw` file** — BWT/FM-index - **`.meth.mbw` file** (optional) — BS-seq index, generated when *Generate BS-seq index* is enabled
## Algorithm choice
By default, minibwa uses the **libsais** algorithm for BWT construction, which is fast but requires ~18N bytes of RAM (where N is the genome length). For large genomes on memory-constrained systems, enable **low-memory BWT-SW** to use a slower but much more memory-efficient algorithm.
## BS-seq mode
Enable *Generate BS-seq index* to produce an additional `.meth.mbw` file that combines C-to-T and G-to-A converted reference genomes for directional bisulfite sequencing alignment.
@ATTRIBUTION@
